image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a turtle resting on rocky ground. The turtle has a dark, high-domed carapace with visible scute patterns and some lighter yellowish markings. Its head is extended, showing a pointed snout and small lateral eyes. The skin on the neck and limbs appears rough and textured. The front left limb is visible, appearing stout with claws. The background is blurred natural terrain.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, proportionally large relative to the shell opening, with a distinct pointed snout and small eye on the side of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Carapace is high-domed and oval, dark brown to black with a smooth, slightly glossy surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shell exhibits a high dome and oval shape. The color is dark brown/black with a sheen indicating a smooth/glossy texture, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Carapace has three longitudinal keels in juveniles that become less prominent with age.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While there are ridges along the scute seams, the distinct 'three longitudinal keels' characteristic of juvenile mud turtles are not clearly defined as separate raised ridges running the length of the shell; the shell appears more uniformly domed or the keels are very worn/indistinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plastron is small and yellowish with two hinges allowing partial closure.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The turtle is viewed from a top-side angle; the plastron (underside) is completely occluded by the body and substrate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is grey to brown with a rough, scaly texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the neck and legs shows a rough, wrinkled, and scaly texture with grey-brown coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet and sharp claws.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible front limb is short and stout. Claws are visible. Webbing is difficult to confirm definitively due to the angle and dirt, but the general morphology matches.
The tail is not visible in this frame; it is likely occluded by the rear of the shell or the angle of the photo.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No ability to fully retract into shell due to small plastron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral/functional trait that cannot be verified from a static image where the head is extended.

The connection between the front right limb and the body/shell is somewhat ambiguous and muddy. The anatomy of the shoulder joint seems to blend into the shell edge without clear definition, suggesting slight structural fusion or melting.
